sentences.text:
Smt. Jogdibai vs Prakash on 31 March, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Ind:8435
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Indore

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Binod Kumar Dwivedi

On The 31st Of March, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 2259 of 2019
 Smt. Jogdibai And Others
 Versus
 Prakash And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Manish Jain - Advocate for the appellants.
 Shri Manoj Jain - Advocate for respondent No.3 / Insur
 Order

This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 07/01/2019 passed by I Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sardarpur, District Dhar (M.P.) in MACC No.21/2018, whereby an amount of Rs.8,57,500/- has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition i.e. 01/02/2018 to the appellants / claimants / survivors of the deceased Gulabsingh with interest @ 6% per annum, who died in a road traffic accident occurred on 01/11/2017.

entities.text: I Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sardarpur, District Dhar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellants / survivors of the deceased submits that the learned Claims Tribunal has considered the income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- per month only.
At the time of accident deceased was working labourer and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

His contention is that in case the income of the deceased is not proved by any cogent evidence, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8435 2 MA-2259-2019 income ought to have been assessed on the basis of circular issued by Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh under the Minimum Wages Act,
according to which income of the deceased on the date of accident comes to Rs.7,125/- per month considering him as 'Unskilled Labourer'.
2.1

entities.text: Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He further submits that the learned Claims Tribunal has awarded a meager amount of Rs.40,000/- only in the head of Loss of Consortium.

His contention is that all the survivors should have been awarded Rs.40,000/- each in the head of Loss of Consortium in the light of para 59.8 of the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 .

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On these submissions, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount.

Smt. Jogdibai vs Prakash on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31614264/
1 3.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal being devoid of any substance.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.

From perusal of the record, it is apparent that at the time of accident i.e. on 01/11/2017 deceased was working as labourer, however, his income has not been established by adducing cogent evidence, therefore, in the light NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8435 3 MA-2259-2019 of the judgment delivered by the apex Court in the case of Chandra @ Chanda @
Chandraram & Anr.

Vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093, income of the deceased is to be assessed on the basis of circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act, therefore, on the basis of circular income of the deceased is taken as Rs.7,125/- per month for unskilled labour.

6. In the case of Pranay Sethi (Supra) , Hon'ble the Apex Court in para 59.8 has held that all the survivors of the deceased are entitled for an amount of Rs.40,000/- each in the head of loss of consortium, therefore, since the claimants are wife and children of the deceased, each of them are entitled for an awarded Rs.40,000/- each in this head.
Adequate amount has been awarded in other heads, which requires no interference by this Court.

7. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:
Rs.7,125/- pm + 25% FP Loss of Dependency: X 12 months - 1/4th Personal Expenses X Multiplier of 14 = Rs.11,22,187/-
 Loss of Consortium: Rs.2,00,000/-
 Loss of Estate: Rs.15,000/-
 Funeral Expenses: Rs.15,000/-
 Total: Rs.13,52,187/-
 MACT Awarded: Rs.8,57,500/-
 Enhanced Amount: Rs.4,94,687/-
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.13,52,187/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.8,57,500/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.4,94,687/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8435 4 MA-2259-2019 Smt. Jogdibai vs Prakash on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31614264/
2 8.

Since the appeal has been valued at Rs.4,00,000/- only, therefore, the appellants are directed to pay additional court fees on the rest of the amount of Rs.94,687/- within a period of 30 days from today at the prevailing slab of court fees, thereafter, the same will be disbursed to the appellants.
Other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest @ 6% shall remain intact.
9. Subject to payment of requisite additional court fees within the aforesaid period, the enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate.

It is made clear, in case the court fees is not paid within the stipulated period, the appellants will not be entitled for claiming interest on the enhanced amount beyond 30 days' period, till the payment of requisite court fees.
10. Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellants / claimants is allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.
(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Tej Smt. Jogdibai vs Prakash on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31614264/
